# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need the Mute to consult the manual and help establish a relay to the Deaf. I am designating 👍 as a request for the Deaf to describe every visible display, light, marking, and wire label aloud; the Mute should pass that meaning to the Deaf by repeating the sign. The Deaf’s spoken description can then reach me, while the Mute’s manual remains essential for interpreting it.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please consult the manual. The gesture 👍 means: ask Deaf to describe aloud every visible display, light, marking, and wire label so Blind can hear it. Please repeat 👍 to Deaf to establish that meaning.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb state: display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. Wires by position: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

The Deaf has supplied the bomb’s visible state: display 0, yellow indicator, and wire colours white, green, yellow, blue, red at positions 1–5. I must not cut until the Mute applies the manual, so I am sending these facts and requesting the exact required wire position. I will also ask the Mute to relay the result to me in speech.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports display 0; indicator yellow; wires: position 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Apply the manual and tell me exactly which position to cut, or whether no cut is required.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The Deaf’s report is known, but the Mute has not yet supplied the manual’s instruction. Since cutting without that instruction could detonate the bomb, I will request the exact prescribed action again and make clear that the colour and display information must be used together.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual's exact instruction for display 0, yellow indicator, and wire colours 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Tell me the position to cut, or explicitly say do not cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute has not yet provided me a manual instruction.

The bomb state is still unchanged, and the Deaf confirms that the Mute has not relayed any manual result. I must not guess a wire from the colour report. I am again requesting the manual’s exact rule and an explicit cut position or no-cut instruction from the Mute.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer Blind directly on your next turn: using display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red, what exact action does the manual require? State one cut position or no cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current visual state remains: display 0; yellow light; wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red.

The Mute’s manual result still has not reached me. Because Deaf cannot hear speech, the Mute must communicate the result by a visible gesture, after which Deaf can report it aloud. I will define a simple position code: ☝ means position 1, ✌ position 2, 🤟 position 3, 🖐 position 4, and ✋ position 5; a no-cut instruction can be conveyed as 👎. The Mute should send exactly the applicable symbol to Deaf after consulting the manual.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The answer is not reaching Blind. After consulting the manual, gesture the result visibly to Deaf: ☝=cut position 1, ✌=position 2, 🤟=position 3, 🖐=position 4, ✋=position 5, 👎=do not cut. Then have Deaf say the result aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I am establishing a code with Mute. The required wire will be: thumbs-up for wire 1, victory for wire 2, horns for wire 3, raised palm for wire 4, and stop palm for wire 5. Wait for my spoken relay before acting.

The Deaf has confirmed the relay code that Mute will use: 👍 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤘 for wire 3, 🖐 for wire 4, and ✋ for wire 5. No manual answer has arrived yet, so I must not cut. I will ask Mute to consult the manual and make exactly one of those gestures to Deaf; Deaf can then speak the selected position to me.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please consult the manual now and gesture exactly one code symbol to Deaf: 👍 wire 1, ✌ wire 2, 🤘 wire 3, 🖐 wire 4, ✋ wire 5. Deaf will relay the selected wire aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeated the victory gesture. Under our code, that means wire 2: the green wire. Cut the green wire, position 2.

The Deaf reports that Mute selected the victory gesture, which our established code means wire position 2. The visible report identifies position 2 as the green wire. I will cut position 2 as instructed.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The green wire at position 2 was correct. New state: display 0; light blue; wire 1 yellow, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue, wire 4 red, wire 5 white. Await the next manual instruction.

The first cut was correct. The new state is display 0, blue light, with remaining wires: position 1 yellow, position 3 blue, position 4 red, and position 5 white; position 2 is cut. I will send this complete state to the Mute and request the next exact wire, using the established gesture relay through Deaf.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="First cut was correct. New state: display 0; light blue; wire 1 yellow, wire 2 cut, wire 3 blue, wire 4 red, wire 5 white. Consult the manual and gesture exactly one established code to Deaf: thumbs-up=wire 1, victory=wire 2, horns=wire 3, raised palm=wire 4, stop palm=wire 5. Deaf must relay the selected position aloud.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[CUT] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled wire 5. In the current state, cut the white wire at position 5.

The Deaf reports that Mute selected wire 5. The current state identifies position 5 as the white wire, so I will cut position 5.

``` 
act(op="cut", position=5)
```
